title: TerminalFix Attack Uses Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA to Deploy Reverse Tunnel Into Corporate Networks
content_md: The attack begins on compromised websites displaying a convincing fake Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA. The page shows a “Verify you are human” prompt, Cloudflare branding, and a loading animation. When users click the verification box, a malicious PowerShell command is copied to their clipboard. They are then told to open Windows Terminal or PowerShell and paste the command to complete the fake verification. The command appears legitimate because it displays Cloudflare-themed messages, including a false confirmation that the user is not a robot. In reality, it downloads a ZIP archive, extracts it into a hidden directory under C:\ProgramData , and launches a batch file. TerminalFix Opens Reverse Tunnels The archive contains a legitimate signed Windows executable named LockScreenContentServer.exe and a malicious dui70.dll file. The attackers abuse DLL sideloading by placing the malicious DLL alongside the legitimate executable. When launched, the trusted executable loads the attacker-controlled DLL instead of the genuine Windows component. The sideloaded DLL starts the next stage of the infection. It downloads PNG images from attacker-controlled domains and extracts hidden malware from their pixel data. Fake Cloudflare Turnstile verification displayed on a compromised website (Source: microsoft) This steganography technique helps disguise the payloads as harmless image files and makes network inspection more difficult.
